verses.text: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat at the home of a prominent Pharisee. Everyone there was watching him closely.
A man suffering from swelling was in front of him.
Jesus asked the legal experts and Pharisees, “Is it allowed to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
But they stayed silent. Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.
Then he said to them, “If your child or ox falls into a well on the Sabbath, which of you wouldn’t pull them out right away?”
They couldn’t answer him.
Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, so he told them this story:
“When someone invites you to a wedding feast, don’t take the place of honor. Someone more distinguished than you may have been invited,
and then the host who invited both of you will come and say, ‘Give this person your place.’ Then you’ll have to move down in disgrace.
Instead, when you’re invited, take the lowest place. Then the host may come and say, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ That will bring you honor in front of everyone at the table.
For those who lift themselves up will be brought down, and those who humble themselves will be lifted up.”
Then Jesus said to his host, “When you give a lunch or dinner, don’t invite your friends, brothers, relatives, or rich neighbors. They may invite you back, and you’ll be repaid.
Instead, when you give a feast, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind.
Then you’ll be blessed, because they can’t repay you. You’ll be repaid when the righteous are raised.”
When one of the people eating with Jesus heard this, he said, “Blessed is the one who will feast in God’s kingdom!”
Jesus replied, “A man prepared a great dinner and invited many guests.
At dinner time, he sent his servant to tell them, ‘Come, everything is ready now.’
But they all began making excuses. The first said, ‘I bought a field and need to go see it. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I bought five pairs of oxen and need to try them out. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I just got married, so I can’t come.’
The servant came back and reported this. The angry homeowner told him, ‘Go quickly into the streets and alleys of the town and bring in the poor, disabled, blind, and lame.’
The servant said, ‘Sir, I’ve done what you ordered, but there’s still room.’
The master said, ‘Go out to the roads and country lanes and urge people to come in, so my house will be full.
I tell you, none of those who were invited will taste my dinner.’”
Large crowds were traveling with Jesus. He turned to them and said,
“If anyone comes to me and doesn’t hate their father, mother, wife, children, brothers and sisters—even their own life—they can’t be my disciple.
Whoever doesn’t carry their own cross and follow me can’t be my disciple.
Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. Won’t you first sit down and figure out the cost to see if you can finish it?
Otherwise, if you lay the foundation but can’t finish, everyone who sees it will make fun of you,
saying, ‘This person started building but couldn’t finish.’
Or what king going to war against another king won’t first sit down and consider whether he can meet the enemy’s twenty thousand soldiers with his own ten thousand?
If he can’t, he’ll send a delegation while the other king is still far away and ask for peace terms.
In the same way, none of you can be my disciple unless you give up everything you have.
“Salt is good, but if it loses its flavor, how can it be made salty again?
It’s not useful for the soil or the manure pile; it gets thrown away. Anyone with ears to hear should listen.”
